nodes.label: ledger-margin-analysis project
nodes.rationale: An analysis toolkit, not an application; ships with no real data. Two independent freight-analysis pipelines (cost/margin and routing), neither assuming the other has data, because real freight ledgers so far have had either costed invoice lines or vehicle trip logs, not both.

nodes.label: Cost/margin analysis pipeline
nodes.rationale: Loads/validates a raw invoice-ledger export, cleans with every decision logged, allocates costs under multiple pluggable strategies to compute true per-transaction margin, slices margin by customer/route/month, and checks whether an apparent pattern survives an obvious alternative explanation.

nodes.label: Routing (dead-head / utilisation) pipeline
nodes.rationale: Loads a vehicle trip log (no cost data), detects dead-head (empty-running) legs against a distance matrix, quantifies vehicle utilisation, and prices empty km at an explicit, caller-supplied diesel rate. Built to run independently of the margin pipeline.

nodes.label: src/schema.py
nodes.rationale: Every column name is referenced through schema constants everywhere else in the codebase - a schema change is a one-file edit.

nodes.label: OVERHEAD_SCHEMA
nodes.rationale: The pool of cost that isn't attributable to any single transaction; margin.py's allocation strategies distribute it across transactions.

nodes.label: schema.COLUMN_ALIASES
nodes.rationale: Maps common real-world header variants (e.g. veh/truck -> vehicle_id, from/to -> origin_id/destination_id) to canonical names so a differently-headed real export is still recognised.

nodes.label: src/synth.py
nodes.rationale: Generates synthetic ledger+overhead data, or trips data (--mode trips) - pure noise, no planted pattern - used to exercise every code path before real data arrives.

nodes.label: src/clean.py
nodes.rationale: Runs five named steps, each appending to a decision log (step, rows affected, rule applied); clean(df) returns (cleaned_df, decision_log).

nodes.label: src/margin.py
nodes.rationale: Exposes three interchangeable strategies (margin.STRATEGIES) sharing signature (ledger_df, overhead_df) -> df, so allocation logic is swappable without touching callers.

nodes.label: src/confounder.py
nodes.rationale: Each function returns a comparison table so you can check whether an apparent pattern is actually explained by mix, by one entity, by a volume/rate shift, or by payment timing.

nodes.label: src/detect.py
nodes.rationale: Inspects a file's columns and decides which pipeline(s) can run, using schema.COLUMN_ALIASES so a differently-headed real export is still recognised.

nodes.label: src/pipeline.py
nodes.rationale: CLI entry point for both pipelines, or --auto + src/detect.py. Fails loudly (raises) if a cleaned file doesn't pass schema.validate() - it does not write output that looks fine but isn't.

nodes.label: dashboard/app.py
nodes.rationale: Renders up to five views across both pipelines, each independently: missing one pipeline's data skips only that pipeline's views with a plain message, not a crash. No analysis logic of its own - every number comes from src/margin.py, src/slice.py, or src/routing.py.

nodes.label: notebooks/01_explore.ipynb
nodes.rationale: Margin + routing usage examples, executed with real output.

nodes.label: tests/test_routing.py
nodes.rationale: Tests src/routing.py against hand-built fixtures with known answers; the same fixtures are used to verify dashboard/standalone.html's JavaScript matches the Python originals.

nodes.norm_label: make targets (synth, synth-trips, clean-data, clean-trips, test, dashboard)

nodes.label: data/reference/distances.csv (placeholder matrix)
nodes.rationale: Committed distances.csv is placeholder data for synthetic location IDs (LOC001-LOC010) only, illustrative km values with no relationship to any real road network. Must be rebuilt with actual road distances (via a routing API like OSRM/Google Distance Matrix or manual lookup) before running on real data - running the real analysis against the placeholder file will silently produce meaningless km/empty-cost figures, or meaningless km attached to the wrong locations if IDs coincidentally collide.

nodes.label: dashboard/index.html (interactive margin dashboard)
nodes.rationale: Runs entirely in the browser against a precomputed snapshot of data/synthetic/ledger.csv - switching strategy or Top N re-renders instantly, no server involved. Mirrors dashboard/app.py's five views but does not read live data.

nodes.label: DATA (precomputed strategy snapshot)
nodes.rationale: Embedded JSON snapshot with kpis/by_customer/by_route/by_month for each of the three margin strategies, plus concentration and dataQuality (excluded transactions/months).

nodes.label: STRATEGY_EXPLANATIONS
nodes.rationale: Explains the data-quality footnote per strategy: for proportional_by_revenue/per_unit_by_quantity, transactions with no allocated cost fall outside the overhead file's covered months, a consequence of ambiguous D/M vs M/D dates in the source export resolved day-first by clean.py's stated policy - their margin sums to $0 in those months, not a real collapse.

nodes.label: dashboard/standalone.html (Freight Empty-Running Tool)
nodes.rationale: Self-contained HTML/CSS/JS routing tool - opens in any browser, no install, no server. Nothing is uploaded anywhere - all parsing and computation happens on-device. Only implements the routing pipeline; a cost-shaped file gets an honest 'not implemented here' message rather than a fabricated margin computation.
